newsitem.title: CANADA: Texaco Canada eyeing ELAN bid-report.
newsitem.headline: Texaco Canada eyeing ELAN bid-report.

text.p: Texaco Inc unit Texaco Canada Petroleum Inc could be formulating a takeover bid for struggling Canadian heavy oil producer ELAN Energy Inc, a report published on Friday said.

Texaco Canada, which has heavy oil operations near ELAN's in the Elk Point area of northeastern Alberta, was planning to tie the acquisition in with the construction of a heavy oil upgrading facility, Canada's Daily Oil Bulletin reported, quoting industry sources.
"The guys are working on it pretty hard right now," one was quoted as saying.
"Of course ELAN's been shopped pretty hard too. Whether they can do the deal or not remains to be seen but they are doing the evaluations."
ELAN Chief Executive Verne Johnson was not available for comment on Friday.
But analysts contacted by Reuters said the deal, which would be valued at at over C$530 million at ELAN's current stock price, would make sense for both companies.
"That actually wouldn't surprise me at all," said one Calgary-based industry analyst. He had not heard of the potential marriage before.

Texaco Canada sold its stake in British Columbia natural gas concern B.C. Star Partners in early March, prompting speculation at the time that it planned to reinvest the funds in a heavy oil acquisition. Heavy oil producer Wascana Energy was in play after a hostile bid from Talisman Energy Inc.
ELAN is a partner in the ECHO heavy oil pipeline in northern Alberta with Gibson Petroleum Co Ltd, which the Daily Oil Bulletin quoted it source as saying was 36-percent Texaco-owned.
ELAN's stock price has slid since June, when the company revealed that efforts to increase production were faslling short of expectations.
ELAN sank to a low of 7.90 after an analyst released a report outlining the production woes and what he believed was a grim outlook.
However, the price has climbed steadily this week and closed on Friday at 9.95, up 0.50.
The company adopted a poison pill in early June as its production problems began to mount. Johnson told Reuters at the time that he believed ELAN was vulnerable to a bid.

The report did not specify whether a deal would be friendly or what the offer price would be, although analysts told Reuters a bid would have to be well above C$10 a share. ((Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
